about.h1: About PeptideLabIndex and our editorial standards
about.intro: PeptideLabIndex compares research-peptide shops on facts we can check: lab reports, measured content, portal verification and listed prices per mg. Reviews are written by the PeptideLabIndex Editorial team. On {date} we audited {shops} shops and opened {reports} lab reports.
about.whoP1: All reviews, rankings and guides are written and checked by the PeptideLabIndex Editorial team. We publish under the team name and do not claim medical, legal or laboratory credentials.
about.whoP2: We do not test samples ourselves. Our expertise is reading what shops and labs publish and putting it side by side in the same format.
about.indepH: Independence: scores never depend on commission
about.indepP1: Some shops are affiliate partners. They pay us a commission when a reader buys through our link. The score formula is the same for every shop, partner or not.

privacy.description: Privacy policy of PeptideLabIndex: cookieless Plausible analytics without personal data, affiliate links that set cookies on shop sites, and email contact.
privacy.intro: Short version: we do not set cookies and do not collect personal data on this site.
privacy.anaP: We count page views with a self-hosted Plausible Analytics instance. It does not use cookies, does not store IP addresses and does not build user profiles. We only see totals such as page views and referring sites.
privacy.affP: Links marked "Visit" go to partner shops. When you click one, the shop's own site may set a cookie to record that you came from us. That cookie is set by the shop, under the shop's privacy policy, not by this site.

privacy.mailP: If you email us, we use your address and message only to reply. We do not add it to a mailing list.

faqs.q: How do you rank research peptide shops?
faqs.a: Each shop gets a 0-5 audit score from six parts: lab verification (30%), fill accuracy (20%), test panel depth (20%), entity transparency (15%), dispatch information (10%) and value per mg (5%). Rankings on this site use that score only, never commission.

faqs.q: What does "portal-verified" mean?
faqs.a: The lab report could be found on the testing lab's own website, not only as a file on the shop's site. {portal} of the {reports} reports we opened were portal-verified.

faqs.q: Why do some shops have no "Visit" button?
faqs.a: Only partner shops get an outbound store link (an affiliate link). Other audited shops are still scored and listed, with a link to our review page only.

faqs.q: Do you give dosing or health information?
faqs.a: No. All listed products are sold as research-use-only laboratory reagents. We compare lab reports, listed prices and shop transparency only.

faqs.q: Which lab is best?

title: How We Score Research Peptide Shops (Methodology)
description: How we score shops: six weighted parts, a 0-5 score and {reports} lab reports opened on {date}. No paid placements. See the method.
m.h1: How we score research peptide shops
m.intro: Every shop gets a score from 0 to 5. It is a weighted average of six parts, led by lab verification (30%) and fill accuracy (20%). We read public shop pages, lab reports and lab portals on {date}. We did not place test orders, and commission never changes a score or a ranking.

faqs.q: Do you buy products and send them to a lab?
faqs.a: No. This audit reads what shops and labs publish. We did not place test orders, so we cannot confirm what an individual parcel contains.

faqs.q: Can a shop pay for a better score?
faqs.a: No. Partner shops pay commission on sales made through our links, but the score formula is the same for every shop. Rankings sort partner shops by score only.

faqs.q: How is price per mg calculated?
faqs.a: Listed price divided by the mg on the label. If a sale price is shown, we use it. We do not apply discount codes and we do not convert between EUR and USD.

faqs.q: How often is the data updated?
faqs.a: The current data set was read on {date}. Each page shows the date of the last check.

m.partsH: The six parts of the score
m.partsP: Each part is rated 0 to 10 by the auditor, with a written reason on every shop page. The weighted average is divided by two to give the 0-5 score.

part.labVerification: Does the shop publish lab reports, and can we find them on the testing lab’s own website? Reports that only exist as files on the shop’s site count less than reports we could look up on the lab portal.
part.fillAccuracy: How close is the measured amount to the label? We divide measured mg by label mg on every opened report. 100% means the vial holds exactly what the label says.
part.panelDepth: Which tests do the reports cover? Purity only scores lower than purity plus measured mg, identity (mass spectrometry), endotoxin, sterility or heavy metals.
part.entityTransparency: Does the shop name the company behind it, with an address or registration number, on its own pages?
part.dispatchReliability: Does the shop publish where it ships, how fast it dispatches and which carriers it uses?
part.valuePerMg: How does the listed price per mg compare with other audited shops? If a shop does not publish prices, this part is left out and the other weights are scaled up.

title: Vial Stock Concentration Calculator (mg/mL)
description: Laboratory stock concentration calculator (mg/mL) for single and two-compound research vials, with an optional measured-mg input. Research use only.
calcp.intro: Works out the stock concentration in mg/mL from the mass in a vial and the volume of diluent added. You can use the measured mg from a lab report instead of the label. For in-vitro laboratory work only; no dosing or usage information.

faqs.q: How is stock concentration calculated?
faqs.a: Stock concentration (mg/mL) = mass in the vial (mg) divided by the volume of diluent added (mL). Example: 10 mg in 2 mL = 5 mg/mL.

faqs.q: Why enter the measured mg from a lab report?
faqs.a: The measured amount on a lab report can differ from the label. In our audit, opened reports showed measured content above and below the label amount, so the measured figure gives a more exact concentration.
